source_text: Icrrur secundum magnitudinem non est cognoscere Deum ; impossibile est enim mensurari Patrem ; secundum autem dilectionem ejus, hee est enim que nos per Verbum ejus perducit ad Deum, obedientes ei semper discimus quoniam est tantus Deus, et ipse est qui per semetipsum constituit, et elegit, et adornavit, qui est secundum nos. Et nos igitur cum his que continentur ab eo, factisumus.
pass_a_gloss: It is not to know God according to magnitude; for it is impossible to measure the Father; but according to His love, for this is what leads us to God through His Word, obeying Him we always learn that God is so great, and He Himself is who establishes and chooses and adorns through Himself, who is according to us; and therefore we, with those things which are contained by Him, have been made.
pass_b_english: Knowing God by measuring His magnitude is impossible, for no one can measure the Father. But His love leads us to God through His Word, and as we obey Him we always learn how great God truly is. He Himself establishes, chooses, and adorns all things through Himself—He who relates to us—and so we, together with everything He contains, have been made.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and the specific meaning of 'secundum magnitudinem' and 'secundum dilectionem ejus'. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the theological agency and causal relations of the source.
